tools.name: host_file
tools.description:
Add a file to your hosted site. The file goes live immediately at the site's public URL.
Each upload creates a new version in the site's history.

Supported: HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, images (PNG, JPG, GIF, SVG, WebP), fonts (WOFF, WOFF2, TTF)
Max: 10MB per file

tools.name: get_hosted_files
tools.description: Lists the files in a hosted site's current version.

tools.name: host_zip
tools.description:
Upload a zipped bundle of files to a hosted site in a single call.
Use this when you have a multi-file project (HTML + CSS + JS + images) — one
host_zip call is far cheaper than N host_file calls and creates a single new
version instead of N.

`zipContent` is the .zip file's bytes as standard base64

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "build_website" is 3535 chars, far longer than this server's median (700). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: build_website, get_site_status · Private data: build_website, host_site, host_file, get_hosted_files, host_zip · Public sink: build_website, host_file, host_zip · Destructive: build_website.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: build_website, get_site_status · Private data: build_website, host_site, host_file, get_hosted_files, host_zip · Public sink: build_website, host_file, host_zip · Destructive: build_website

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "build_website" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
